plan.english: Sky and Earth lay in darkness. Nothing was bright. Then great Sky spoke. "Let light come to be!" A young goddess was born from him. The gods were astonished. She stood up, and lit up the settlements. Her radiance is dear to the eyes. Men saw her and became glad. The father set a famous name for her. Her name is Dawn. Her brightness is imperishable.

A great serpent dwelt in a deep hollow. It crept out of the hollow, and swallowed the sun, and darkness covered the settlements. The men became afraid. Then the eagle went up. He seized the serpent and split it. The serpent died. Blood came forth from it. Forth came the sun, and it dawned. They caught sight of it and became glad. They gave the eagle a gift. The eagle's name is famous.

Dawn drove her own cattle to the wide field. A thief seized the cattle and drove them into a hollow. Then Dawn did not shine, and it was getting dark. Then her dear dog sought the cattle and found them in the hollow. He ran to her. She arrived at the hollow. The thief trembled, and fled. She freed the cattle, and led them out into the clearing, and light flashed up.

title: The Broken Wheel of the Sun

plan.english: The wheel of the sun broke. Then it spoke: "Father Sky, behold my wheel!" The twins heard his voice and came. The swift horses stood, and were astonished. It was getting dark. They put the wheel in order, and they yoked the swift horses. It became whole, and became strong. It went again, and light arrived. The twins are dear to us.
Night and Dawn were sisters. Night was walking on the earth. Then Dawn followed her own sister, and glowed red, and was young. Night saw her coming and fled. The sisters did not know each other.

Sky and Earth lay together. Sky is father, and wide Earth is mother. The gods were born from them. Then the gods stretched Sky out above, and made Earth stand below. Now light goes between them, and comes down. Between them stands the oak, and the oak is thick. Men dwell there.

It was getting dark. Night arrived, and men lay down. Then the sun became tired, and sank into the deep water. Sleep seized it, and it travelled in a ship through the night. Then the young goddess arrived there, and said: "Stand up!" It woke. She clothed it in radiance. It dawned.

title: The Shepherd and the Bright Woman

plan.english: A shepherd led his own sheep to the wide field. Then he saw a woman. She was wearing bright clothing. Then he said: "Who are you?" "I am Dawn. I go forth, and the sun follows me." He became afraid, and fell down on his knees. Then she said: "Do not be afraid!" The shepherd's heart became glad. But she gave the shepherd gold and wool. His sheep are many.

Thick snow lay on the oak, and the wolves arrived at the settlement. Men sat at the fire. Then spring arrived, and it became warm. The snow melted, and ran. They vanished. The men left the settlement and led their animals to the wide field. The women cooked the nourishing food. The birds built nests in the oak. Warm weather is good for them.

title: The Eagle Looks at the Sun

plan.english: The eagle was going upwards. He kept looking at the sun with his own eyes. Then it spoke to the eagle: "Who looks at me?" He spoke: "I look at you. My eyes do not tremble, and I am not afraid." Then the sun knew the eagle, and set a famous name for him. The eagle is the king of birds.

There was no fire for men, and they became cold. Then a young woman looked up at the sun. "Give us fire!" It heard her, and let it go. She seized it and carried it to the village. They gave the woman a gift. They sat at the fire, and became warm. She cooked the nourishing food at the fire, and they ate. The woman's heart is satisfied. The woman's fame is imperishable.

A king was walking in the mist. A dog followed him, and he went astray. The mist was thick. He trembled. Then he cried out: "Give light!" It dawned, and the mist fled. Then he saw the light, and entered the village. He gave Dawn a ram. She gave him good fame. Then he built a shelter for her.

Dawn took the yoke, and yoked the swift horses. The sun sat down in the chariot, and drove them. Its wheel glowed. She protected them. The horses spoke: "Where are we going?" Dawn spoke: "Go forth, and carry light to men!" Then the horses went, and were not afraid, and it dawned.
A man made a pledge. Sky heard it, and caught sight of it. But the man deceived his brother. Then he died. The wolves ate him. Whoever deceives a brother, the sun sees him. He does not live.

Dawn, bright goddess, Daughter of Sky! You shone for us, and darkness fled from you. Men caught sight of you and became glad. You are young, and you are imperishable. You are the sister of the night. Your radiance is dear to the eyes. Give us good fame, dear one! Give us imperishable fame!

Dawn, dear mistress, you lead out the cattle. You clothe yourself in bright clothing. The birds rise when you come. You give us gold. You give wool to the shepherd. Give us sons and rams! Give us imperishable fame, mistress!
Sun, eye of Sky! You who know the hearts of men, you who yoke the swift horses, you who warm the animals, you who melt the snow, you who ripen the grain, shine for us again, give us light!

title: Hymn of the Wheel of the Sun

plan.english: The wheel of the sun goes in the sky. Swift horses draw it. It lights up the settlements. May the wheel not break! May the swift horses not stand still! Splendor goes in front of it. Radiance sits in the chariot. May the light of the sun, indeed, be dear to us.

Father Sky, giver of good things! You who set a famous name for Dawn, you who made dear light for us: you have stretched out above us. You are the king of the gods. Hear us, hear our words! Protect our animals and our fire!

Sky and Earth, the great mother! The gods were born from you. You are wide, and you are deep. You nourish the male animals and the lambs. Between you stands the oak. Hear us, parents! Protect our sons and our dogs!

Light is first. Light, indeed, is dear. Light splits the great darkness. Light is the eye of the gods. In the light men live. In the darkness, indeed, they tremble. Brightness and radiance are the sons of light. May the dear radiance not leave us! May splendor come to our shelter!

Night and Dawn, great sisters! Night, you go away, and you, mistress, follow her. You glow red, and the birds rise. Night, indeed, you bring darkness. Mistress, you bring dear light. Protect us, sisters, in the night!

Let us speak good words to Dawn. She is coming, and the birds rise. Let us give her a gift. Let us listen to her voice. She glows, and the shepherd drives the animals. We are alert. We have seen the light, and we became glad.
Father Sky, when you rain, the grain grows. The many cattle drink the water. The beasts are thirsty. Rain on our field! May the water come, and may the grain grow up!
Dawn is first, and the sun follows her. She goes before, and it comes after. She glows, and it is dear to us. We, indeed, rise when they come.

Spring has come, and it became warm. The snow melts, the water runs. The women cook the nourishing food. The wolves vanish. The birds build nests. Bright one, may you be dear to us. May we live in your light!

Who is she, the young one who comes from the sky? She is Dawn, the dear goddess. Where does she go, and where does she stand? She goes, and the sheep follow her. Who was first to see her? The shepherd was first to see her. May the dear goddess shine for us!

Dear goddess, come to us! Shine for us, and may the darkness flee. May we see the light, and may we not die. Give us a long life and good fame. May our household be bright with splendor! Drive the thief and the wolf away from us. May our fire burn in the shelter. May our heart, indeed, be glad in the light.

Dawn, I lead my own sheep to the wide field. Protect them, indeed, from the wolf! May the wolf not come to them! May my sheep be many. May they live a long time, and may they not die. May my dear dog see the wolf. May none be missing. I shall give you wool, dear goddess.

Sun, I am going away from my village. Go before me, and look upon me! May the wolf and the thief not seize me! May my knees not tremble. May my heel not slip. May I not be afraid. May I arrive at home, and may I be whole.

Father Sky, we give you a ram. Take it, and give us water! We shall bring you wool and gold. We are thirsty, and our animals are thirsty. Rain on our fields, and may the grain grow up! May our animals, indeed, not die.

Dear mistress, my son lies, and has become warm. Remember my son! Look upon him and guard him! May my son stand up, and may he not die. May he drink water, and may he eat. I shall give you a lamb, mistress.
We have seen the light, and we became glad. Bright one, you gave us light. We give you a gift. Come to us again. We are satisfied. May our good words be heard! Be dear to us, do not leave us!
Young mistress, I am seeking a wild beast. Lead me and look upon me! Show it to me, and may it not flee. May my eyes catch sight of it. May I seize it, and I shall give you a gift.
Sky, hear! Sun, see! I have indeed made a great pledge. If I deceive a friend, may Sky kill me. If I do not deceive him, may I live.

Sun, we are going to war: go before us! Guard us, and may we overpower the enemies. May the many enemies flee from us. Rescue us from the enemies! Give us many prizes! May we arrive at the fire, and may we not die.

Dawn, give me a son! May he become strong, and may he live a long time. May he be a hero. May he be free. May his name be famous. May he eat nourishing food, and may he be sated. I shall give you a lamb and wool.

I am the great king of the village. Dawn, Sun and Sky, protect my settlement! May my men live a long time. May their sheep be many. May the thief not come to my village. May there be much grain in the settlement. Give me imperishable fame!

It is getting dark, and night is coming. Sun, you sank into the water below. Father, guard us in the night! May we lie down, and may sleep seize us. May our dog guard the shelter. May the oak cover us. May we wake, and may we see the light again.

I am ploughing my wide field. Sky, rain upon it! Sun, warm it! Mother Earth, give me grain! May my grain grow up, and may I eat. May the birds not eat it. May my yoke not break. May Perkwunos not strike me.
